t: Section 6 of said Act of April 1, 1942, is amended by striking out the words “The salary of the chief judge shall be $9,500 per annum and the salary of each associate judge shall be $9,000 per annum” and substituting in lieu thereof the following: “The salary of the chief judge shall be $14,500 per annum and the salary of each associate judge shall be $14,000 per annum.”

fable.w: This section only amends a prior Act to raise the salaries of a chief judge and associate judges. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any decision.
fable.s: The salary of the chief judge shall be $14,500 per annum and the salary of each associate judge shall be $14,000 per annum.

qwen_block.w: This section merely sets the salary amounts for federal judges. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process involving parties outside the federal government. There is no public comment period, advisory board with outside members, or right to sue granted here.
qwen_block.s: The salary of the chief judge shall be $14,500 per annum and the salary of each associate judge shall be $14,000 per annum.

opus.w: This section only amends the salary amounts for the chief judge and associate judges. Nothing brings outside parties into a federal decision through consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies or a right to sue. Mentioning judges and courts does not grant anyone a right to challenge a federal decision, so this is not participation.
opus.b:
**Step 1.** The only possible trap is the word "judge," which suggests court proceedings and so the right to sue. But this section only raises judges' salaries. It sets no hearing, consultation, comment period, advisory body or right of action, and no one outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

**Step 2.**

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends the statutory salary levels for federal judges. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government in the decision-making process. The change is a direct legislative mandate regarding compensation, not a procedural requirement for outside input.
qwen_chat.s: Section 6 of said Act of April 1, 1942, is amended by striking out the words “The salary of the chief judge shall be $9,500 per annum and the salary of each associate judge shall be $9,000 per annum” and substituting in lieu thereof the following: “The salary of the chief judge shall be $14,500 per annum and the salary of each associate judge shall be $14,000 per annum.”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing salaries affects judges, who are outside the executive branch, but this is a legislative adjustment of compensation, not a process of consultation or participation by outsiders in a federal decision. The section contains no mechanism for public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with non-federal entities.
